sample.name: 2d-arcade-game-design
sample.description: Design, audit, and polish lightweight 2D arcade, mobile arcade, browser canvas, Phaser, PartyKit co-op, and tic-tac-toe-like casual games. Use when improving game feel, controls, feedback, juice, readability, difficulty curves, short-session loops, multiplayer room play, touch controls, or satisfying audiovisual/haptic polish for simple 2D games.

sample.name: 2d-game-ui-design
sample.description: Comprehensive, framework-agnostic principles for designing 2D game UI - menus, HUDs, buttons, dialogs, inventory screens, pause screens, settings, notifications. Covers spacing systems, sizing scales, touch targets, typography hierarchy, button states, motion/juice, feedback loops, theming without dictating colors, accessibility, and platform-specific rules (mobile/desktop/controller). Use this whenever Looza is designing, reviewing, or critiquing UI for any 2D game (Sleepy Game Room, XO, Star Squad, or any future game project), whenever he asks for UI/UX feedback on a game screen, or whenever he's about to prompt another AI (Codex, etc.) to build game UI and wants a spec to hand off. Trigger on words like "game UI", "HUD", "menu design", "button feel", "game screen layout", even if he doesn't say "skill" explicitly.

sample.name: aesthetic-intelligence-engine
sample.description: A universal aesthetic judgment system for taste, beauty, composition, and artistic direction in any medium (UI, graphics, video, writing, sound, architecture, objects). Use when the output will be seen, heard, or felt and the default look would be generic, or when asked for taste, art direction, or "make it look/feel right". Skip for purely functional work with no perceivable surface.

sample.name: afterburn
sample.description: Design, build, critique, or refine distinctive modern interfaces with task-led UX, creative direction, anti-template visual craft, and bounded verification. Use for product UI, websites, apps, landing pages, and components; not backend-only work or general factual lookup.
